source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-76: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 76 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume an authorized, isolated test allocation and record hardware, PCIe/NVLink and NUMA topology, GPU/NIC affinity, link state, driver/firmware/runtime/container versions, peer-access capability, IOMMU and container permissions, buffer placement, registration and pinning, process affinity, message sizes, concurrency, clock and thermal state. Treat unknowns as unknowns and distinguish measured facts from estimates; do not infer GPUDirect use from a benchmark name or speed alone.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 76: with direct-path use independently verified and all placement, workload, clocks, concurrency, and duration controls matched, GPU-direct RDMA improves steady-state bandwidth (GB/s) and/or reduces host CPU utilization versus a host-staged baseline, without worsening p50/p95/p99 latency, completion/error rate, or checksum correctness beyond predeclared limits. Measure registration/setup separately from transfer; report latency in microseconds, bandwidth in GB/s, CPU percent, error counts with denominators, repeated trial distributions, and uncertainty.

Start with read-only discovery, capability and permission checks, then a minimal correctness test before performance. Run direct and staged cases interleaved or randomized on the same topology and workload, synchronize timestamps, and capture independent evidence of the selected path plus queue/completion and checksum results. For troubleshooting, isolate topology, permissions, registration, affinity, transport, and fallback in that order; for design/performance/tool-use variants, preserve the same gates and matched baseline. A failed capability, registration, link, queue, or correctness gate stops the comparison rather than proving a performance regression. Only explicitly approved reversible changes are allowed; roll back on corruption, link instability, new completion errors, thermal/power breach, or a predeclared latency/error threshold. Redact identifiers and never expose credentials.

quality_dimensions.measurement_plan: matched randomized direct-versus-staged trials with units and uncertainty

risks: A staged fallback can be mistaken for GPUDirect RDMA without independent path evidence.
Topology, permission, registration, affinity, or link failures can confound comparisons.
Diagnostics may expose infrastructure identifiers and require redaction.
evidence_required: topology, affinity, capability, permission, registration, and path-selection artifacts
exact hardware/software configuration and workload/buffer details
synchronized bandwidth, latency, CPU, error, and correctness measurements with denominators
predefined rollback threshold and approved change record
domain-expert review
